pages.name: Montreal's Sabbat: The Three-Way Power Struggle

text.content: Since the execution of the infernalist Archbishop Sangris in 1992, Montreal's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} has fractured into three factions vying for control of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}'s oldest North American Sabbat bastion. Archbishop Carolina Valez, a Mexican-born @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} imposed on the city by Cardinal Strathcona and backed by her pack the Lost Angels, holds official power but is widely (and wrongly) perceived as weak due to her distaste for excessive public violence. Alfred Benezri leads the Shepherds of Caine, Montreal's oldest and most scholarly coven, who consider Valez a mere transitional figure and want to restore the city's traditional theocratic order. Ezekiel, a young Black Hand-affiliated firebrand and secret childe of Sangris, commands the violent pack 25:17 and the ultraviolent Les Orphelins and Wretched, and would rather see Montreal burn than watch anyone else claim it. Each faction is unaware that the true threat to the city is neither political rival: it is Metathiax, the Decani demon still imprisoned within Mount Royal.

pages.name: The Temple of Eternal Whispers (Communal Haven)

text.content:
Montreal's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} communal haven, the Temple of Eternal Whispers, occupies a vast underground necropolis beneath what is now Dorchester Square in downtown Montreal, built up over two centuries from the colonial-era graveyards of Ville-Marie. Cardinal Strathcona expanded it dramatically during the cholera epidemic of 1832 (secretly caused by Metathiax's infernal servants) into a proper subterranean mausoleum, kidnapping and torturing the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} architect François Dumas to design its Gothic-Classical halls; Dumas was rewarded for his masterwork with eternal torpor sealed inside his own tomb.

The haven is named for the soft, ceaseless moans that echo through its vaulted halls — the voices of cholera victims buried alive by frightened mortal doctors, whose screams the Sabbat have come to treasure, holding a yearly Halloween rite in which they bury kidnapped children alive to keep the tradition (and the hauntings) alive. Unbeknownst to nearly everyone, these whispers actually carry Metathiax's voice, slowly driving more Sabbat toward the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.rR0qLGz3CPcibovj]{Path of Evil Revelations}.

Key chambers include the Mausoleum (the temple's 500-vampire-capacity central hall, seat of the archbishop's bone throne and the Lost Angels' lair), Caine's Chapel (housing shrines to each Path of Enlightenment and the bronze Gates of Eternity leading to the Alexandrium library), the Crypts (claimed piecemeal by individual packs as lairs), the above-ground Church of the Forsaken (housing Montreal's "black grove" of mortals transformed into moaning trees by a Shepherd Thaumaturgical ritual), and Dumas' sealed tomb deep in the temple's forgotten tunnels.

pages.name: The Litany of Blood and the Librarians

text.content: Created in the 18th century as the Liber Defunctorum to honor @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} who died establishing a foothold on Montreal, the Litany of Blood grew under the Shepherd Soeur Marianne into the definitive record of the sect's fallen heroes and genealogies, drawing on missionary reports that also became the foundation of the wider Sabbat's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.db3Fhvpv32rhN3Mm]{Path of Caine} theology. When Marianne retired into isolated contemplation, her Noddist aides formed the Librarians coven to maintain the Litany and the associated Alexandrium library, accessible through the bronze Gates of Eternity in Caine's Chapel. The Librarians remain Montreal's premier scholarly coven, closely allied with the Shepherds of Caine, and count among their number Christanius Lionel (the city's foremost Path of Caine scholar), Béatrice L'Angou, Marie-Ange Gagnon, Ellen Conlynne, and the deranged oracle Jacob the Glitch.

"The Heart" is the lair and public face of the Widows, Montreal's Cathari coven, built from the burned-out ruins of the original 1800s-era Widows' brothel by its current leader, the Rose. The Widows offer their services as mistresses and dominatrices to Montreal's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} elite and even to visiting @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} or curious Shepherds, always guaranteeing absolute discretion — a discretion that fuels persistent rumors of clients who never left. The Rose's private chamber is an elaborate torture/pleasure suite; her covenmates Creamy Jade and Black Lotus (Nina Barker) each keep their own macabre studios within.

pages.name: Saint-Joseph's Oratory (Lair of the Shepherds of Caine)

text.content: Since the 1920s the Shepherds of Caine have made their lair in the crypt beneath Saint-Joseph's Oratory, completed in 1955 at the foot of Mount Royal in honor of the mortal faith-healer Frère André. The Shepherds hoped to Embrace André as a successor to their founder, Saint Ignace, but he refused and was allowed to die peacefully; his heart, kept beating in a vat of vampiric vitae, remains on display in a dark alcove and retains a potent connection to the city's aura of faith. The coven's hidden chambers form a circular network beneath the resting place of Frère André's remains, centered on a prayer chamber used for the coven's Nocturnal Redemption rites, including the annual Feast of Twelfth Night marking Saint Ignace's Embrace.

pages.name: The Blood Circle and Decani's Fountain

text.content: The Blood Circle, located beneath a dilapidated tenement in Old Montreal, is the original ground consecrated by the demon Metathiax's first mortal acolyte, Terrence DeBouville, in the 16th century, and remains the primary site of infernal worship on the island. Blood spilled within the circle instantly becomes diseased; Metathiax's infernalists drink it to imbue themselves with virulent plagues they then spread among Cainites and mortals alike. On the anniversary of Metathiax's imprisonment, infernalists gather for a rite called Decani's Fountain, bathing in brackish poison that oozes from the circle — a ceremony that only the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} antitribu Pierre Bellemare currently knows how to lead.

The Douglas Mental Hospital is the haven of Les Misérables, a mad coven whose incomprehensible rites and worldview are so bizarre that an invitation to witness them is considered among the rarest of privileges in Montreal's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}. The coven keeps Toy, a feral, quadriplegic @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.JTrvDnw1eqZyHKuH]{Samedi} who has become the unofficial mascot of Montreal's Sabbat and the centerpiece of numerous cruel games played at his expense (and occasional, dim enjoyment).

Mount Royal, the wooded hill at the heart of the island, is Montreal's most dangerous and mysterious ground — the literal prison of the demon Metathiax, its trees and earth infused with his malign influence. Cainites buried on its slopes as part of Creation Rites almost never survive the night, either perishing outright or emerging twisted into feral, disease-spreading monstrosities that serve as Metathiax's unwitting hounds. The Metro stations along the mountain's north side (Line Four) are known among the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} as unusually strange, sometimes disgorging malformed creatures that prey on lone Cainites. Only a handful of individuals — notably Raphael Catarari, Jacob the Glitch, and Erinyi — are known to have survived a Creation Rite there.

Montreal's extensive network of Metro stations, shopping malls, and connected office buildings gives the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} an entire nocturnal world beneath the streets, expanded deliberately by Archbishop Véronique La Cruelle with hidden maintenance tunnels linking the transit system to the communal haven. McGill Station and the downtown core are popular gathering points after the trains stop running at 1:30 a.m. Feeding is treated as an art form by most covens (following Véronique's example), from elaborately staged mock-hauntings to games such as Bobbing for Mortals, Fatality Fun, Gray Cup Football, and Playing in Traffic. Popular nightspots include the Sabbat-run bars Heaven, Angel's Fall (home to the band Wyldchylde) and The Heart, alongside Zarnovich's traveling circus and the abandoned Cinema V on Sherbrooke Street, used for Sabbat movie nights.
